name: 0H10M1ke
bio: 0H10M1ke is a Brooklyn-based interdisciplinary artist known as “The One-Line Master,” recognized for creating more than 15,000 live portraits and light-based performances across cities including New York, Miami, Tokyo, Kyoto, and Berlin. Working at the intersection of drawing, performance, and light, he translates real-time gesture into luminous forms using a Wacom tablet and stylus, treating each mark as an immediate, unrepeatable response to the moment. His ongoing series L1ght Graff1t1 Make0vers transforms participants into vivid, reimagined identities through live digital light performance, blending street aesthetics, improvisation, and spectacle. Across international exhibitions at venues such as the Park Avenue Armory, the Guggenheim Museum, and the Museum of Graffiti, his work explores light as both medium and metaphor for connection, impermanence, and shared human presence.

name: Aérosculpture
bio: Inspired by airships and the dream of flight, Jean-Pierre David creates immersive artworks that explore the possibilities of aerostatic forms, light, and movement. Since the mid-1990s, he has developed inflatable sculptures, aerial performances, and illuminated installations that combine suspended performers, giant puppets, music, and visual spectacle. As advances in LED technology enabled light to become an integral part of his work, he expanded into increasingly sophisticated creations that merge digital systems, electromechanics, transparency, and motion. His large-scale installations invite audiences into imaginative worlds where art, technology, and the wonder of floating converge.

name: Ana Tomashvili
bio: This Georgian artist works at the intersection of architecture, sound, and moving image, reimagining buildings and public spaces through light, projection, and immersive soundscapes. Their practice transforms static structures into dynamic, emotional environments that invite audiences into moments of awe and heightened perception. Rooted in a fascination with wonder and presence, their work uses synchronized light and sound to slow time and expand sensory awareness. Through a blend of architectural precision and poetic rhythm, they create immersive experiences that encourage reflection and a renewed connection to the beauty of the surrounding world.

name: Beamhacker
bio: Beamhacker is a light installation artist whose practice explores the space where technology meets imagination and strives to spark curiosity and transform human perception. With roots in the events industry, his early work embraced a lo-fi, set-design aesthetic before evolving into more complex, technology driven artworks that merge DIY electronics with cutting-edge systems. His installations have employed LED, fibre optics, lasers, video projection, VR, and interactive sensors to create immersive environments that blur the boundary between the physical and the imagined.

name: Big Art
bio: Big Art exists to ignite imagination and wonder through large-scale, interactive, and immersive public art installations. With a purpose rooted in inspiring creativity, we craft experiences that captivate audiences, spark curiosity, and transform public spaces into vibrant playgrounds for exploration. Our team designs, builds, and tours robust, safe, and unforgettable installations across North America, whether through our existing catalogue or custom commissions.

name: Black Art Speaks
bio: Black Art Speaks (BAS) is a Cincinnati-based nonprofit, membership-driven artist collective dedicated to promoting Black culture, social justice, and creative expression through the elevation of Black artists' voices. Founded in 2020, the organization brings together artists, community leaders, and advocates who use art as a catalyst for dialogue, healing, and community impact. BAS is best known for creating Cincinnati's iconic Black Lives Matter mural and has since developed numerous public art initiatives, exhibitions, educational programs, and professional development opportunities for Black artists. Through collaboration, advocacy, and public art, Black Art Speaks continues to foster cultural awareness, create economic opportunities for artists, and strengthen communities throughout Greater Cincinnati.

name: Brett Bolton
bio: Brett Bolton is an audiovisual artist from Las Vegas who creates tightly connected musical and visual systems and then controls them live with drums and a touchpad. Every drum hit, synth line, and ambient swell is tied directly to a visual element, allowing each AV song to be as dynamic, improvised, and imperfect as the human that drives it. Given the real-time generative nature of the AV systems he builds, every performance is a completely unique collaboration between computer and human that exists only in that moment and can never be perfectly replicated. When he’s not building personal work, Brett designs visuals and real-time systems for touring pop artists, XR stages, and cutting-edge venues.

name: Cedric Michael Cox & Studio 181 Brent Keltch
bio:
Cedric Michael Cox creates vibrant paintings that fuse abstraction and recognizable imagery into rhythmic compositions inspired by music, nature, architecture, and art history, ranging from cubist geometric forms to surreal cityscapes and floral-like environments. Brent’s bio: Brent Keltch is a multifaceted Cincinnati-based visual artist, sculptor, and gallery owner. Operating out of Studio 181 at the historic Essex Studios colony in Walnut Hills, his work blends diverse artistic disciplines with community advocacy.

CEDRIC: https://www.instagram.com/cedric_michael_cox?igsh=MW05Mm9rdmZjc2FsYg

name: Chase Melendez
bio: This artist’s work is formally inspired by the aesthetics of early video games, 1980s and 1990s cartoons, and cinema, with a focus on color, background art, and narrative-driven visual storytelling. They have developed a personal visual language called “Candy Pop Sci-Fi Abstraction,” using it as a framework for worldbuilding through vibrant color combinations, sharp geometric forms, and layered compositions. Their work spans painting, object-based surfaces, and immersive installations that aim to activate space, reimagine overlooked environments, and create playful, energetic visual experiences for the public. Raised in the Pacific Northwest and currently based in Cincinnati’s Camp Washington neighborhood, they hold an MFA from the University of Cincinnati and a BA from San Diego State University, alongside experience in event production, film, and theater.

name: Chaske Haverkos
bio: Chaske Haverkos is a director, immersive designer, 3D animator, and projection-mapping artist from Cincinnati, Ohio, whose work spans advertising, creative production, and experiential entertainment. A graduate of the University of Cincinnati’s DAAP program, he brings over 15 years of experience collaborating with clients, organizations, and public entities to create visually rich and technologically driven experiences for audiences of all sizes. His practice fuses traditional design principles with emerging technologies, combining animation, motion graphics, and projection mapping to craft immersive audiovisual environments. Working as a freelance artist, he continues to explore the digital frontier of light and sound, developing experiential works that translate artistic vision into dynamic, spatial storytelling.

name: Christo Squier & Thomas Blackburn
bio:
Christo Squier is a composer, installation artist, and creative director whose work explores the intersection of music, science, and immersive experience. Drawing on fields such as particle physics and cognitive science, he creates generative environments that investigate perception, energy, and the boundaries between the tangible and intangible. His practice blends electronic and classical composition with installation, performance, and interactive systems, and he has collaborated with companies including Punchdrunk, Secret Cinema, and Les Enfants Terribles. He has also received commissions from Science Gallery London and Britten Pears Arts, along with awards for innovation in immersive sound.

Thomas Blackburn is a creative code and audiovisual specialist with over 20 years of experience designing and programming complex audiovisual systems for performance and installation. His work spans technical production, visual art, and custom instrument design, supporting large-scale immersive projects. He has collaborated with artists including Aphex Twin, Grace Jones, Amon Tobin, and institutions such as Tate Modern and FOLD, focusing on pushing the boundaries of audiovisual performance through technology.

name: Columbus college of art and design
Custom Fibre Optics Ltd
bio: Custom Fibre Optics Ltd creates immersive light installations inspired by natural forms and systems, using fiber optic lighting to evoke mycelium networks, plant life, and flowing water. Working intuitively with each environment, they design installations that feel organically connected to the spaces they inhabit, from forest floors and gardens to public events and gathering places. Their work transforms ordinary settings into magical experiences that inspire wonder, curiosity, and reflection. Through light, they encourage audiences to notice overlooked beauty and foster deeper connections with the natural world and one another.

name: Daniel Rossa
bio: Daniel Rossa is a German media artist whose practice operates at the intersection of digital and physical space, creating immersive audiovisual works that dissolve the boundaries between the two and invite new forms of environmental perception. Trained at Bauhaus University Weimar, Rossa draws on an interdisciplinary background in media art, technology, and science to transform architectural structures into dynamic canvases of light, motion, and narrative. His award-winning project, 555 Kubik, reimagined a museum façade as a living, dreamlike entity, using projection mapping and optical illusion to explore the idea of architecture reflecting on itself. By centering each work on the unique qualities of its site, Rossa uses light and imagery to engage buildings as active participants in storytelling, revealing the tension between physical structure and ephemeral intervention.

name: Daniel Shields
bio: Daniel Shields is a Kentucky-based installation artist currently living outside of Cincinnati, Ohio who has used soft yarn to create immersive pieces that cover or enclose large outdoor areas since 2014, but who has only taken art seriously since 2019. Typically, his creations are, at their core, public art which manipulates innate perception of well-known locations in largely unconscious ways by segmenting and dividing 3D space with simple, sparse lines. Most installations use fluorescent acrylic yarn with UV light and UV lasers to create vibrant effects that trick the senses. Some woven installations are visitor-created, where yarn balls are provided and anyone can add their own elements, creating a truly democratic experience where signs read “please touch the art.” Like people and the relationships between them, yarn is seemingly fragile but can be stretched thin and made to endure a tremendous amount of stress without breaking – but there is a limit to everything, and strength in numbers.

name: DecideKit
bio: DecideKit is a motion graphic design firm situated in Bangkok, Thailand, with a lot of passion. We are committed to the craft of motion graphics and use data-driven insights to reach a variety of audiences with powerful messages. Our specialty is in offering complete motion graphic solutions for a variety of media platforms, such as projection mapping, immersive art, 3D screen, concert, infographic and product launch. To develop visually appealing audience experiences, DecideKit combines passion and competence in data-driven design.

name: Drew Merritt
bio: Drew Merritt is an American painter and muralist known for his striking realism and his ability to merge classical aesthetics with contemporary urban environments. Beginning his career nearly three decades ago as a graffiti writer in New Mexico, he has since created monumental murals across the United States and internationally, working with brands and organizations such as Tesla, Adidas, UFC, Converse, and Virgin Hotels. His work often juxtaposes Renaissance-inspired portraiture with modern settings, exploring themes of empathy, vulnerability, and time while translating fine art realism to architectural scale through spray paint and latex. Alongside his mural practice, he maintains a fine art studio practice in oil painting, exhibiting work in galleries worldwide and bridging the worlds of street art, fine art, and cultural storytelling.

name: Dulk
bio: Spanish artist Antonio Segura, Dulk, is one of the most important names in Spanish painting of the moment internationally. His body of work begins to form in urban art and mural painting to which he remains closely linked today along with study work, but does not stop there. He continues to research and constantly create new forms of expression through different media, drawing, sculpture or photography among others. Dulk’s paintings are the immediate byproduct of his travels into remote areas and his memories of a natural wonder and wildlife. He has witnessed first hand both the beauty of these landscapes and the terrible collapse that is creeping over them like a fatal tide. By painting something beautiful he asks audiences to gather the strength to look away from art and toward nature, as painful as that may be. With a strong ecological conviction to defend ecosystems and the most vulnerable species, his work invites the viewer to be part of a unique imaginarium, full of energy and with a special sensitivity to color. A dream world with animals and natural spaces that tells personal, universal and unique stories.

name: Elléna Lourens
bio: South African artist Elléna Lourens began working on personal and collaborative creative projects while in school. Since then she has further pursued illustration, street art, painting and embroidery. Her style lends itself to the past in its representation of ancient symbols, patterns and colour schemes , while voicing an intuitively current aesthetic that resonates and seeks to redefine emotional iconography. She has immersed herself in the creative world, working alongside established artists, as well as furthering her own practice, taking part in shows and creating murals in both South Africa and internationally.

name: Everything Good Studio
bio: Everything Good Studio is a Brooklyn-based multidisciplinary art and design collaboration between Rachel Ciavarella and Jack Kalish, focused on the creative use of emerging technologies. Their practice centers on light as a dynamic and immersive medium, using tools such as digital LEDs and projection to create kinetic, participatory environments that engage audiences directly. They believe art is completed through audience interaction and design their work to challenge perception, inviting viewers to experience the world with a sense of childlike openness and imagination. Through public art commissions and international exhibitions across the United States, Europe, and Asia, the studio creates immersive experiences that explore light as a universal and emotionally resonant force.
notes: Listed in the BLINK artist directory but not by this name in the 2026 participating-artists press release (2026-06-08).

name: Felix Frank
bio: This German digital artist creates mapping and light installations that transform architectural spaces into immersive visual environments. Born in Munich in the late 1970s and educated in Fine Arts in Paris and Motion Design in Barcelona, their practice is shaped by early influences from Waldorf education and the graffiti and hip-hop culture of the 1990s, which first sparked a drive to reshape public space through visual intervention. Today, they work with projection mapping and large-scale light installations, replacing spray paint with projected “light paintings” while maintaining a focus on nighttime urban environments. Their work combines detailed animation with carefully tuned sound design, often incorporating specific frequencies, to create immersive experiences that aim to shift perception and evoke states of harmony and presence.

name: Filip Roca
bio: This media artist works at the intersection of light, architecture, and motion, creating projection mapping and live generative visuals that transform facades into dynamic visual systems. Based between Barcelona and Lisbon, their practice evolved from over a decade in animation, motion graphics, and art direction into large-scale architectural light works presented internationally at festivals and institutions including Fête des Lumières, iMapp, Noor Riyadh, Tokyo Lights, and the Museo Nacional Thyssen-Bornemisza. Treating architecture as an instrument, they use light not as decoration but as structural force, revealing hidden geometries, flow fields, and latent tensions within built forms. Their process combines site data, parametric systems, and tightly synchronized audiovisual composition to create precise, high-contrast transformations that explore themes of structure, transformation, and perception at city scale.

name: GERA 1
bio: This artist’s journey began in 2009 with graffiti in their hometown, later expanding into formal training in painting, drawing, and fine arts studies beginning in 2015. After three years of academic exploration in printmaking, painting, and photography, they began traveling and creating murals across European festivals, eventually holding their first solo exhibition in San Francisco in 2023. Now based in Athens, Greece, their practice draws heavily from photography as a source of inspiration, using captured textures, reflections, and human presence as the foundation for layered compositions. Through painting and mixed-media experimentation across surfaces such as canvas, aluminum composite, and plexiglass, they distort and reconfigure imagery to create vibrant visual worlds where color drives movement, emotion, and form.

name: illumaphonium
bio: This family-led creative team specializes in the design, fabrication, installation, and maintenance of large-scale interactive light art installations around the world. Drawing on expertise in design, engineering, computer science, creative therapies, music, and a proudly neurodiverse perspective, the team creates immersive works that blur the boundaries between art, entertainment, and participation. Their installations prioritize accessibility and human connection, inviting people of all ages and backgrounds to engage through intuitive, collaborative experiences that require no instruction or prior knowledge. Rooted in a belief that art should bring people together, their work fosters creativity, equality, wonder, and shared moments of discovery in public spaces.

name: Inka Kendzia
bio: Inka Kendzia is an award-winning interdisciplinary artist, VJ, and director who uses light, projection, and emerging technologies to explore humanity’s connection to nature and shared experience. Working across VR, AI, and generative visuals, she creates immersive works designed to encourage reflection and collective engagement. As a motion design director and live visual artist, she has produced work for projects including The Beatles: Eight Days a Week and Luciano Pavarotti documentaries, and has directed performances for artists such as Black Coffee, Seal, and Ibeyi. Her collaborations span international festivals, theatres, and institutions, including the Smithsonian Museum of African Art and Everard Read Gallery, as well as award-winning public installations like AD PACEM presented at BLINK Cincinnati.

name: James Bullough
bio: James Bullough is an American-born artist living and working in Berlin, Germany, known for his large-scale murals and studio paintings that merge realistic portraiture with graphic distortion and abstraction. His practice is shaped by a combination of influences, including the raw energy of urban graffiti he encountered growing up in Washington, D.C., and the disciplined study of Old Master oil painting techniques. By combining these contrasting approaches, he creates visually striking works that balance technical precision with expressive disruption. His murals and studio works have been exhibited internationally in galleries, museums, and art fairs, and can be found on landmark walls across Europe, the Americas, and beyond.

name: Jérémie Bellot
bio: Jérémie Bellot is a French architect and visual artist whose practice bridges architecture, digital art, and large-scale projection mapping. Trained in both cinema and architecture, he became a state-certified architect before dedicating himself fully to artistic practice in 2010, co-founding AV-Exciters and later leading AV Extended as artistic director. His work focuses on architectural video mapping and immersive light installations, often created in collaboration with musicians and designers for major cultural events and monuments worldwide. He has served as curator and creative director for projects such as the Constellations de Metz festival and the Château de Beaugency digital art center, and has received multiple awards including the Trophée des Lumières and Cannes Heavent Awards for landmark projection works on sites such as Place Stanislas in Nancy and the Basilica of Zaragoza.

name: Jérémy Oury
bio: Jérémy Oury is a French digital artist and sound designer whose work explores perception, space, and light through immersive audiovisual environments. With a background in sound design for theatre and architectural acoustics, he creates fulldome films, video mapping works, and light installations that investigate the relationship between reality, technology, and consciousness. His practice, presented internationally at festivals and venues such as MUTEK MX, Mapping Festival, ISEA, FILE, Artechouse, and the Paris Planetarium, blends algorithmic visuals and generative soundscapes to construct sensory environments where order and chaos coexist. Through these immersive systems, Oury invites viewers into contemplative experiences that blur the boundaries between digital space and inner perception.

name: Jim Tucker and Frank Young
bio:
Frank D. Young

Frank D. Young is an American fine art photographer whose portraits treat their subjects as living documents of their existence. Though he has always had a camera in his hands, he began his journey as an artist in 2008, building a practice rooted in analog processes and equipment while moving fluidly between film and digital capture. Since 2012, he has documented the Black residents of Cincinnati's Over-the-Rhine, a neighborhood reshaped by economic revitalization and gentrification, creating a portrait record of a community in the midst of change. His clients include the Cincinnati Regional Chamber, the World Affairs Council of America, 1001 Colors, Duke Energy, Mortar, 3CDC, and The City Flea. Drawing on influences from Gordon Parks and Richard Avedon to Carrie Mae Weems, Jamel Shabazz, and Spike Lee, his work bridges documentary tradition and fine art portraiture, framing everyday people with the dignity and permanence of the historical record.

Jim Tucker

Jim Tucker is a British-born artist and educator whose passion is to use art to build community through collaboration and education. Since leaving England in 2007, he traveled extensively before settling in Cincinnati in 2021, carrying with him a belief in "eating what the locals eat," a phrase that signifies reverence and respect for the culture of every new place. He interprets his surroundings through site-specific automatic painting, generating imagery and characters that he contrasts with work inspired by historical and contemporary photography of the area. Since moving to Cincinnati, he has produced and painted over twenty murals, many in partnership with 1001 Colors and now recognized as city landmarks, and collaborated with institutions including the Cincinnati Art Museum, the Marketer Collaborative, and several Big Tech companies. Across a combined career of more than twenty years, his work bridges fine art, murals, and community building.

The Collaboration

Jim and Frank have been working together for several years, with Jim licensing Frank's photographs as references in his paintings and installations. BLINK 2026 marks the first time the two are coming together for a unique hybrid mural, combining a wheat paste of Frank's photography against Jim's painted interpretation of the mural's location.

name: Jonas Denzel
bio: Jonas Denzel (*1990) is a filmmaker and visual artist with a focus on projection mapping, video installation, and documentary film. In 2016, he received a Fulbright Scholarship and studied Film and Media Art at Temple University in Philadelphia. In 2018, Denzel completed his master’s degree in “Time-based Media” with distinction. Commissioned works for public, urban spaces in Leipzig, Chicago and Bucharest among others, followed. In 2021 he won the international video competition IMAPP in Bucharest. As an artist and drummer Jonas‘ goal is to make the audience become part of projections and their locations. He uses rhythms and patterns to create interactive projections. The influence of drums and percussions play an important role in his work.

name: JP Jackson + Brian Havener
bio: Architects by trade, JP Jackson and Brian Havener began their friendship and collaboration while at the University of Cincinnati's College of Design, Architecture, Art & Planning. Although separate paths led them to settle in Nashville and Seattle respectively, JP and Brian's shared work continues through a mutual appreciation for immersive experiences that are shaped by craft and latent material qualities. Their projects often re-imagine the mundane, transforming conventional objects into unexpected spatial encounters. Lighting plays a constant and formative role in amplifying the underlying intention of each work.

name: Juan Fuentes
bio: After studying architecture, he specialized in lighting and digital manufacturing. His multidisciplinary training allows him to fully develop his designs. Juan Fuentes' artistic line is based on perception and geometry, evoking immersive sensations and experiences in the audience, blurring the line between the real and the virtual. He works on his projects within biomimicry, using nature as a source of inspiration.​ In recent years, he has exhibited in Light Art exhibitions around the world, including Madrid, Sydney, Singapore, Vancouver, Brussels, London, Stockholm. In 2021, he received the 40under40 award as one of the top 40 lighting designers in the world.

name: Justin Boh
bio: Justin Boh (also known as Post Humongous) is a Kentucky-based creative director and immersive artist whose work explores the intersection of technology, storytelling, and community engagement. With over two decades of experience leading projects for brands such as Amazon, Disney, Google, Old Spice, Dell Technologies, and Pixar, he combines strategy and emotional narrative to create impactful visual experiences. His installations use projection mapping and generative media to transform public spaces into interactive environments that respond in real time to audience movement and participation. Through these systems, Boh reframes interactivity as a language of connection, turning viewers into co-creators and fostering shared discovery, play, and collective expression.

name: Kasumi Art Studios
bio: This artist’s practice blends physical materials with digital and time-based media to create immersive sculptural and cinematic works that explore how movement, sound, and memory shape perception in public space. Their work spans projection mapping, responsive installations, lenticular prints, and large-scale environmental media, often designed to activate architecture and transform how audiences experience built environments. Sound plays a foundational role in their process, informed by a background as a classically trained musician and collaborations with artists such as Grandmaster Flash, DJ Spooky, and Warren Harris (Hanna), as well as custom scores for experimental film and installation projects. With work exhibited internationally—from Carnegie Hall and the Cleveland Museum of Art to major public projection festivals—their practice consistently investigates memory, identity, and transformation through emotionally resonant, symbolically rich audiovisual experiences that invite participation and reflection.

name: Ke Jyun Wu
bio: Ke Jyun Wu is a Taiwanese media artist whose work exists at the intersection of the virtual and the real, blending engineering, nature, and emotional resonance into immersive digital environments. His practice transforms everyday natural phenomena—such as wind, water, and light—into generative, interactive systems where light, sound, motion, and viewer interaction converge to create subtle sensory experiences. Central to his process is the use of a single poetic sentence as both conceptual anchor and creative constraint, from which he develops digital ecologies that prioritize presence, stillness, and feeling over representation. Through works like his DigiScape series, he invites audiences into reflective spaces that reframe perception and encourage a deeper sensitivity to the world around them.

name: Keep Cincinnati Beautiful
bio: Keep Cincinnati Beautiful is a grassroots nonprofit that has connected people, passion, and place since 1978, fostering community-driven public spaces and environmental stewardship throughout Cincinnati. Since 2009, its team of artists has partnered with neighborhoods, nonprofits, businesses, and volunteers to transform overlooked and neglected spaces into vibrant public art installations. Through this collaborative approach, Keep Cincinnati Beautiful works to reduce blight, increase community pride, promote environmental awareness, and improve quality of life for residents across the city.

name: Kemper Sauce Studios
bio: Kemper Sauce Studios is a Cincinnati based engineering and arts collective with an inventive spirit and a whole list of bad ideas. Ultimately, our goal is to bring communities together by providing fun and memorable experiences in the form of large scale light based art installations.

name: Koros Design Studio
bio: This creative practice develops immersive light-based installations that explore the intersection of nature, technology, and human perception. Combining digitally generated designs with experimental materials such as lightweight inflatable fabrics, the team creates walkable environments that encourage both reflection and play. Their work uses light as both a sculptural medium and a metaphor for connection, transforming spaces while inviting audiences to engage with the world in new ways. By blending tactile materials with digital innovation, they create experiences that celebrate the harmony between natural phenomena, emerging technologies, and the human spirit.

name: Kyle Eli Ebersole

name: Lawrence Malott - FOREALISM
bio: Forealism is a father-and-son creative duo consisting of Lawrence and Thomas Malott, working across DJing, costume design, performance art, music, and visual installations. Their multidisciplinary practice blends sound, movement, and handmade, often recycled materials to create immersive, otherworldly experiences centered on audience engagement and personal expression. A defining element of their work is the integration of light through reflective, illuminated costumes and their signature DJ installation, the “Light Ship,” which extends their performative process into a shared space with audiences. Since forming in 2012, they have performed internationally at venues and festivals including the Cincinnati Art Museum, Riverfest, Art Basel Miami, and LIV Miami, while continually evolving their practice between music production and live performance.

name: LeMonde Studio
bio: LeMonde Studio is a multidisciplinary creative practice that designs and produces large-scale, light-based installations that bring people together through play, energy, and collective wonder. Our work exists at the intersection of art, design, and technology, transforming light into a medium for connection and storytelling. Based on collaboration and innovation, we partner with local musicians, visual artists, and engineers to create experiences that respond to human interaction and the rhythm of community life.

name: Leslie Epsztein
bio: Leslie Epsztein is a French designer from Bordeaux who specializes in projection mapping. After studying art, performing arts, and visual communication in France, she spent five years working with video artist Xavier de Richemont before launching her independent practice in 2015. Since then, she has created and contributed to large-scale light installations for cities and festivals across Europe and the United States, blending themes of time, space, science, dreams, and mythology with local cultural narratives. Drawing on her background in illustration, cinema, and graphic design, her work combines painterly and graphic visual styles with a strong emphasis on storytelling and musical rhythm.

name: Lightborne
bio: Lightborne is a creative-led design, animation, & production studio specializing in visuals for tours & live events, commercial & branded content, and installation & immersive experiences. Our studio works as a fully integrated creative partner, uniting specialists in motion design, animation, live-action production, experiential media, graphic design, projection mapping, and large-scale technical execution. Our disciplines work together with intention, precision, and a creative vision that defines our work, ensuring each project invites audiences into an experience that feels purposeful, engaging, and enduring. It would be our honor to participate in BLINK once again. We put all of our hearts into it each year and it means the world to us, the city and the region.

name: Lindsay Glatz + William Nemitoff
bio: Lindsay Glatz is a visual storyteller dedicated to bringing wonder and vibrancy into public space, often drawing on themes of childhood and nostalgia to explore human connection. William Nemitoff, founder of Curious Form, combines expertise in materials, construction methods, science, and technology to develop innovative collaborative artworks and public installations. Together, their studio practice bridges art, architecture, and fabrication, transforming ambitious concepts into built realities through precise craftsmanship and digital fabrication. Their work—especially in light-based installation—merges advanced technology with hands-on making to create striking, durable environments that invite wonder, interaction, and connection.

name: Looking Up Arts
bio: This collaborative practice creates sculptural light installations that transform public spaces into immersive environments for shared discovery, blending art, engineering, and community engagement. Nearly all components are fabricated in-house, combining digital fabrication with hands-on craft to produce works that feel both precise and deeply human. Each project begins with a site and evolves into a responsive environment shaped by movement, sound, and participation, using light as both material and metaphor. The team’s origins trace back to a formative public artwork that shifted their focus from gallery-based work to community-centered installations, leading to a long-term partnership between Sri and Josh that merges technical expertise, scientific principles, and sculptural design into experiential works that invite connection and wonder.

name: Marie AJRAS
bio: Maria AJRAS is an Argentine muralist and visual artist currently based in Brooklyn, New York and working internationally across Argentina, Mexico, Europe, and the United States on large-scale public art projects. Her practice is rooted in the belief that art can reveal what is not yet visible, treating murals as collective thresholds where memory, identity, and emotion emerge into form through color, scale, and gesture. With a background in psychology, she approaches each work through deep listening and community dialogue, translating local narratives into poetic visual compositions that balance realism and abstraction. Her murals—often depicting monumental female figures—function as acts of visibility and reparation, transforming architecture into emotionally resonant spaces that reflect both personal and collective experience.

name: Max Sansing
bio: Max Sansing is a Chicago-based fine artist and one of the city’s most prolific and talented muralists. His distinct aesthetic fuses the color-drenched dynamism of street art with the technical elegance of photorealism. Born and raised on the South Side by two artistic parents, Sansing discovered his passion and creative gift at an early age. During his youth he was involved with several graffiti crews and taught himself oil painting before completing formal training at the American Academy of Art. In addition to his studio practice, Sansing is frequently commissioned to create large-scale murals and experiential installations across the country. He is deeply committed to supporting his Chicago community and is involved with numerous youth programs that expand arts opportunities in underserved areas. His work has been featured in gallery shows and special events in Chicago, New York, and Miami among others.

name: MEDIANERAS
bio: Medianeras is an artistic duo formed by architect Vanesa Galdeano (Argentina–Spain) and visual artist Analí Chanquía (Argentina), who have collaborated for more than fourteen years on large-scale public art projects. Their practice is rooted in the concept of “medianeras,” or side walls, which they reinterpret as spaces that connect rather than divide, using murals to foster connection, belonging, and collective identity within urban environments. Through color, geometry, and architectural sensitivity, they transform city walls into reflective surfaces that engage in dialogue with their social and spatial context. Working internationally across more than 20 countries, their large-format murals merge precision and human scale, turning public space into a site for visual rhythm, interaction, and shared experience.

name: Miami University
bio: At Miami University in Oxford, Ohio, the Immersive & Reactive Media Lab (MUXR) brings together students of design, animation, and creative technology to produce professional-scale media experiences. Operating within the Emerging Technology in Business & Design (ETBD) program, the lab functions as both classroom and production studio, where students gain hands-on experience in projection mapping, motion design, lighting integration, and real-time media systems. Each year, advanced students in the IMS 440 course sequence collaborate with entertainment industry partners, working in professional pipelines alongside studios such as Silent Partners Studio, XR Studios, Cour Design, and 4Wall Entertainment, and building pathways toward careers at leading companies in the field.

name: Mike Stasny
bio: Mike Stasny creates large-scale sculptures, inflatables, and installations that channel joy, absurdity, and a sense of childlike wonder. His work invites audiences into playful, immersive experiences that prioritize feeling and curiosity over fixed meaning, encouraging people to reconnect with creativity and awe. Rooted in the belief that fun can be a radical act, Stasny’s practice uses silliness and spectacle as tools for connection in a culture often driven by productivity over presence.

name: Mindscape Studio
bio: Mindscape Studio is an award-winning multidisciplinary creative studio specializing in projection mapping, immersive experiences, event design, and interactive installations. Blending art, technology, and storytelling, the studio transforms architectural spaces into dynamic, multisensory environments that engage audiences through light, motion, and sound. From concept development to final execution, Mindscape Studio has created works for leading international festivals and cultural events, including Fête des Lumières, iMapp Bucharest, Festival of Lights Berlin, LUMA Projection Arts Festival, and the George Enescu Festival.

name: Napoleon Maddox
bio: The artist’s interdisciplinary practice brings together multiple forms of production to explore subconscious dimensions of intimate relationships, colonial legacies, and acts of liberation. Visual art and object-making have been central to their life since childhood, shaped by parents who used creativity as both a problem-solving tool and a means of sustaining family life, even while questioning its viability as a profession. This tension informs the work as both an act of resistance—asserting presence and voice as a person of African descent—and as a continuation of inherited, resourceful making strategies. Working across painting and mixed media, the artist feels a particularly strong connection to repurposed and recycled papers, layering new narratives over materials already marked by prior stories, while drawing deeply from childhood memories and a lifelong relationship to nature and Southern agricultural heritage.

name: Onda Studio
bio: Onda Studio is a new media art collective based in Italy working at the intersection of art, architecture, and technology. Led by Marcello Arosio—an architect, multimedia artist, and artistic director of Kernel Festival and AreaOdeon—the studio brings together visual designers, musicians, developers, and architects to explore how light, sound, and movement can shape shared human experiences. Their practice examines the relationship between people and digital art across physical and virtual dimensions, bridging the individual and collective through immersive installations and interactive environments. Through video mapping, light, lasers, sound, and mobile interfaces, Onda Studio transforms public space into participatory, living canvases that invite audiences to engage with and reflect on the interconnected systems that shape contemporary life.

name: Paper Acorn
bio: Jessica Wolf creates ceiling-suspended kinetic sculptures inspired by the vastness and patterns of the natural world, crafting immersive environments that evoke wonder, peace, and a sense of uplift. Using lightweight materials such as polycarbonate and synthetic paper, her sculptures balance strength and grace through movement and translucency, allowing light to cast ethereal shadows that transform her organic forms into dynamic, meditative experiences.

name: Parker Heyl
bio: Parker is an installation artist, kinetic sculptor, educator, and mechanical engineer whose work explores the relationship between physical objects and digital technologies in art, music, and architecture. Through kinetic sculptures and immersive environments, he examines what is lost when experiences are translated into digital form, emphasizing the presence and aura of physical objects. Trained as a carpenter and currently teaching at the Bartlett School of Architecture at University College London, he combines technical expertise with artistic inquiry to create thought-provoking electromechanical works. His installations and set designs have been presented internationally at leading galleries, festivals, and cultural events, including the Venice Biennale of Architecture, Munich Biennale, Salon del Mobile Milan, and Coachella Music Festival.

name: Pastel
bio: Francisco Diaz Scotto is a painter and architect (UBA) whose practice approaches public space through the concept of “urban acupuncture,” activating overlooked or neglected sites within the city. Working primarily in facades and other “non-places,” he transforms these surfaces into canvases that engage in dialogue with their surrounding environment. His work draws inspiration from resilient urban flora—plants that grow in sidewalk and wall cracks—using them as symbols to question rigid, exclusionary systems of urban design. By enlarging and recontextualizing these overlooked natural forms, he challenges modern notions of control in architecture while emphasizing a respectful, site-responsive relationship between artwork and environment.

name: Polina Soloveichik
bio: Polina Soloveichik is a Berlin-based artist and muralist born in Russia and raised in the United States. She studied illustration at Pratt Institute in Brooklyn, where she first began painting murals and discovered a passion for creating art in public spaces. For more than 20 years, murals have been at the core of her artistic practice, allowing her to transform spaces and engage directly with communities. Her work can be found on walls large and small throughout Europe and the United States. Through site-specific projects, she explores the unique relationship between art, place, and the public.

name: Radius Concepts
bio: Radius Concepts is a design and fabrication studio specializing in furniture, sculpture, and architectural components for commercial and residential spaces, while also creating immersive public installations that transform ordinary environments into surreal experiences of light, humor, and communal play. Using materials such as steel, foam, sound, and illumination, the studio reimagines everyday interactions as moments of wonder, curiosity, and connection.

name: Scott Pennington
bio: Scott Pennington is a Baltimore-based artist specializing in large-scale participatory installation and sculptural assemblage works. Drawing upon his background as a furniture and cabinet-maker, Pennington utilizes woodworking and construction techniques to create colorful, detailed works of art that engage varied audiences and invigorate public spaces. Pennington’s work suggests a tangible, yet illusory reality that examines labor, consumer culture, the pursuit of simple pleasures, and the construction of nostalgic human connections both genuine and fictitious.

name: Sean Van Praag
bio: Sean began his career in 2008 after earning a degree in digital art and design and joining renowned film title artist and director Kyle Cooper at Prologue in Los Angeles. After honing his skills in film, commercial, and animation work, he launched his own studio, where he continues to work as a director, designer, and animator. His diverse client portfolio includes Nike, Greenies, Exxon Mobil, Left 4 Dead, and artists including Justin Bieber, Jay-Z, Katy Perry, Pitbull, and Fitz and The Tantrums. Since 2013, Sean has increasingly focused on projection art, creating commissioned work for festivals including Digital Graffiti and eight other projection art festivals across the country. His vibrant, playful artwork embraces experimentation and reflects the energy and stimulation of today’s digital world, with the goal of creating something novel that makes viewers smile.

name: Sew Valley
bio: Sew Valley is a Cincinnati-based nonprofit collective of designers, patternmakers, prototypers, samplemakers, and sewists who create immersive, large-scale textile installations using repurposed materials. Their work combines craftsmanship, sustainability, and storytelling, transforming everyday fabrics into dynamic environments that engage audiences through texture, color, movement, and light. By integrating illuminated textiles, projection surfaces, and interactive design elements, Sew Valley creates memorable experiences that foster curiosity, connection, and community engagement.

name: Shahzia Sikander
bio: Born in Lahore, Pakistan in 1969, Shahzia Sikander trained in traditional miniature painting during a period when the medium was largely out of favor with younger artists under the military regime of Muhammad Zia-ul-Haq. She earned her B.F.A. in 1991 from the National College of Arts (NCA) in Lahore, where she studied under master miniaturist Bashir Ahmad and later became the first woman to teach in the Miniature Painting Department. During her time at NCA, she emerged as a pioneering figure within the discipline, challenging its technical and aesthetic boundaries, with her early work The Scroll (1989–90) receiving major national recognition and awards that helped elevate the medium within contemporary art discourse. She later moved to the United States to pursue an M.F.A. at the Rhode Island School of Design, followed by participation in the CORE Program at the Glassell School of Art, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston.

name: Silent Partners Studio
bio: As directors, designers, producers, and creatives, they specialize in visual storytelling, with two decades of experience creating imagery across every facet of the entertainment industry. Operating as a fully integrated design and production studio, they develop cutting-edge stagecraft for both in-person and virtual experiences, spanning music videos, world tours, television, theater, runway shows, sports and esports events, brand activations, corporate presentations, museums, and large-scale installations. Working from ideation through installation, they collaborate closely with clients to create bespoke turnkey and à la carte solutions that merge creative direction, production, set design, and content integration. Their practice is rooted in exploring the intersection of art and technology, using tools such as TouchDesigner, Notch, Unreal Engine, and generative AI to create immersive, interactive environments that invite audiences to actively engage within evolving spatial experiences.

name: Smash Studio
bio: SMASH is a boutique, Stockholm-based experience design studio that creates large-scale projection mapping and interactive installations, blurring the boundaries between technology and architecture. Rooted in music, visual design, and motion graphics, the studio uses light, shadow, and sound to transform public spaces into shared, living experiences. Its collaborative team includes Ash Reed (Design Director), Veronica Reed (Account Director and Project Manager), Emile Pascoe (Lead Technical Artist), and Jonas Johansson (Lead Technical Director), who together shape the studio’s creative direction, technical development, and client relationships. Through real-time graphics, motion design, and custom interactive systems, SMASH develops emotionally resonant environments that invite audiences to engage, explore, and participate, turning architecture into dynamic canvases for collective experience.

name: Sofles
bio: Russell Fenn, better known as Sofles, is an Australian graffiti artist originating from Brisbane. Self-taught, he has been honing his skills for over 20 years, exploring various mediums such as spraypaint, acrylic, drawing and brush painting, as well as digital and illustration works.

name: Spencer Sterling
bio: Spencer Sterling is a multidisciplinary artist and machine learning researcher whose work transforms musical experiences into immersive visual environments. His practice explores the dialogue between music, space, and light, bridging real-time 3D graphics, artificial intelligence, and laser-based installations. Through his work with Silent Partners Studio, he has created visual content for performances by artists including Beyoncé, Celine Dion, and Muse, while his personal practice focuses on translating internal interpretations of music into spatial form. His process moves from 3D environments into custom-developed AI models and ultimately into dynamic laser installations that trace evolving digital compositions, reflecting an ongoing exploration of how sound can be experienced through light and space.

name: Strangeloop
bio: Strangeloop Studios is a visual content production company focused on working with creatives to explore new media and audience experiences. Their team is composed of animators, designers, producers, writers, musicians, and developers.

name: Susan Kosti
bio: Susan Kosti (Zsuzsanna Koszti), born on September 20, 1986 in Paris, is an award-winning international media artist and art director working globally. Her work explores the tension between humanity, science, technology, and spirituality, with the aim of reconnecting people to their environment through immersive experiences. She began her career in 2010 as a video designer for live events before expanding into music video direction and an internationally recognized short science fiction film. Over time, she has developed a distinctive visual language combining highly detailed forms, graphic design, and animation, with installations presented at major venues and festivals including Moment Factory projects, Tokyo Disneyland, UAE National Day 51, Vivid Sydney, and Blink Festival. In recent years, she has also been invited to collaborate with artists such as Es Devlin and has served as art director for major international pavilions and large-scale projection mapping works across global exhibitions.

name: The Great Paper Massacre
bio: The Great Paper Massacre is an artist whose practice is driven by an ongoing process of experimentation and creative exploration. A member of the Truly Design collective since 2018, their multidisciplinary work spans graphic design, illustration, painting, motion graphics, video, and experimental animation. Centered on collage as both a visual technique and conceptual framework, their practice draws inspiration from music, literature, and punk and Dadaist traditions. Working under the moniker The Great Paper Massacre, they use a deliberately provocative identity to deconstruct and reassemble visual language, investigating how images and ideas function by taking them apart.

name: The Mz.Icar Collective
bio: Mz.Icar Collective is an interdisciplinary group of artists creating bold, community-centered public art that blends storytelling, material culture, and speculative imagination. Their collaborative practice spans murals, sculptural installations, textiles, projection mapping, and immersive environments that invite audiences into experiences of joy, reflection, and belonging. Rooted in deep engagement with local communities and cultural histories, their work amplifies underrepresented voices while exploring how emerging technologies like augmented reality and interactive projection can support cultural storytelling and memory-making. Their projects have been installed across cities including Boston, Brooklyn, Cincinnati, Green Bay, and Philadelphia, and have been featured in collaborations with festivals and institutions such as BLINK and The Roots Picnic.

name: The University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music – Lighting Design & Technology
bio: University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music (CCM) – Lighting Design and Technology prepares the next generation of lighting designers, programmers, technicians, and creative professionals through hands-on, experiential learning. Students gain real-world production experience across theater, dance, opera, film, concerts, and live events while working with industry-standard technology and faculty with extensive professional expertise. As one of the nation's premier performing arts institutions, CCM fosters innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence across the entertainment industry.

name: This is Loop
bio: Loop is the collaborative artistic partnership of artists Harriet Lumby and Alan Hayes. Based in their Somerset studio they have established a reputation for creating large scale experiential installations. With over thirty years combined practice focussing on utilising reflections and illusion at the intersection of technology, science and art this has created a common theme throughout their visually impactful architectural style work. Their installations invite audiences to be engulfed by intense and thought provoking choreographed audio visual journeys. Frequently working collaboratively with sound artists and musicians has helped to elevate their work allowing deeper exploration of ideas and concepts and enhancing the bond between audience members and the works themselves. They have a track record in creating both large scale site specific work as well as touring installations and have successfully done this in both the UK and internationally.

name: Truly Design Crew
bio: Since getting up in train yards and abandoned factories, our production can now count anything from large scale murals to anamorphic artworks and painted basketball courts. The years spent in the fields of graffiti writing, street art and muralism shaped our attitude and allowed us to experiment new forms of visual language. We translate concepts and subjects through geometric abstraction. We have fun with different surfaces, deconstructing shapes and spaces and contaminating them with colors. Our artworks have inhabited walls in cities, museums, private homes and business headquarters in Italy and Europe, as well as in New York, Miami, Hong Kong and Macau.

name: Vamos Animation
bio: VAMOS Animation is a German animation studio founded in 2016, organised as a collective of filmmakers, illustrators, artists, and animators with a strong track record at international film festivals and exhibitions. Bringing together diverse nationalities and cultural backgrounds, the collective approaches each project with a distinctly multicultural lens. The studio specialises in films and installations and, beyond classical animation, actively explores new formats and applications for animated sequences. In video mapping, the team has worked at events such as Berlin Festival of Lights (2023, 2024), the Video Mapping Festival in Amiens and Lille, and the mapping of the “Entrepôt des Sels” in Saint-Valery-sur-Somme (France), as well as projects in Cologne for theatre and other contexts. VAMOS stands out for integrating hand-drawn 2D animation with visual effects that serve the concept, prioritising narrative and social impact over mere spectacle.

name: VIGAS
bio: Vigas is a Brazilian multimedia artist known for his large-scale projections, light installations, 360 projections, and live performances. His practice explores the relationship between art, technology, and the environment, transforming public spaces into experiences that inspire new ways of perceiving both urban and natural landscapes.

name: Vince Fraser
bio: Vince Fraser is a pioneering British Afro-surrealist artist whose work sits at the intersection of digital art, visual storytelling, and cultural reclamation. With a career spanning over two decades, he has evolved from a successful commercial illustrator into a visionary digital artist known for immersive works that reimagine Black identity and heritage through an Afro-diasporic lens. Rooted in Afro-surrealism, his practice explores the spiritual, historical, and mythic dimensions of Black life in the present moment, blending photorealistic detail with African symbolism, surreal environments, and contemporary digital aesthetics.

name: Wayne Horse
bio: Willehad Eilers is a German artist also known under the pseudonym Wayne Horse, whose practice spans painting, drawing, video, and installation. Emerging from the German graffiti scene and later graduating from the Rijksakademie in Amsterdam, he continues to live and work in the Netherlands. His work is characterized by a raw, expressive visual language infused with humor and lyrical distortion, often exploring the bizarre, uncomfortable, and compelling aspects of contemporary human behavior. Through a practice that blends ethnographic observation with surreal reinterpretation, Eilers examines cultural and social norms, transforming everyday scenes into unsettling, poetic reflections on the modern condition.

name: Xavier University Art Department
bio: At Xavier University, the Art Department trains artists and thinkers who are grounded in integrity, intellectual curiosity, and a deep-seated sense of belonging. Innovation leads the curriculum. New materials, new contexts, and new audiences come together to push expectations; and Xavier Art students meet them. Between the traditional concentrations of fine Arts, the innovative Graphic Design Program, and the 3D Animation and Immersive Game Design Program, Xavier Art Students bring professional fluency, a portfolio of substance, and a habit of reflection that sustains careers in galleries, museums, design, education, and beyond.

name: Jacob Kaplan
title: Lighting designer
org: University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music (CCM), Lighting Design and Technology
bio: Jacob is a senior at the University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music pursuing a BFA in Lighting Design and Technology. BLINK marks his senior capstone at CCM and he is excited to continue working on this incredible project. Past CCM credits include: Lighting Designer for "Love Letter" (Poiesis Quartet) and Moveable Feast: Illuminate (CCM Philharmonia). Associate Designer for Student Choreographers' Showcase 2025. Assistant Designer for Cendrillion, Rope, Hansel und Gretel and John Proctor is the Villain.
notes: Member of the CCM student team behind "Echoes of Light" (UC News, 2026-08-08). BLINK has not published an individual page.

name: Lia Lubinsky
title: Assistant designer
org: University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music (CCM), Lighting Design and Technology
bio: Lia Lubinsky is a fourth-year Lighting Design and Technology Major at the University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music. During her years attending UC she has had the opportunity to work on many productions in a variety of roles. She has also had the opportunity to intern at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony in Los Angeles, California in 2025. Lia is grateful to be able to study and pursue her passion, and to learn along-side talented and promising young professionals. After graduating, she hopes to go into concert and festival lighting design and programming. She is very excited for the opportunity to work alongside Jacob Kaplan, Lucy Dunn and Jack Walter for BLINK 2026, and hopes that you stop by and take a look.
notes: Member of the CCM student team behind "Echoes of Light" (UC News, 2026-08-08). BLINK has not published an individual page.

name: Lucy Dunn
title: Assistant designer
org: University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music (CCM), Lighting Design and Technology
bio: Lucy Dunn is a lighting design technician focusing on installation and experience lighting design. Lucy is currently in their final year at the University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music working towards a BFA in Lighting Design and Technology. Lucy is originally from Baltimore Maryland and intends to be east coast based following graduation. During their time at CCM, they have worked on productions as a Assistant Production Electrician, including The Lightning Thief, Midsummer Night's Dream and Production Electrician for The Opera Double Bill and the upcoming Fall Dance Works and Cabaret. This summer they are working as a Design Intern for Lunar Telephone Company, focusing on installation projects. Outside of lighting design, Lucy enjoys painting in watercolor and acrylic, hiking, as well as jewelry making and clothing upcycling.
notes: Member of the CCM student team behind "Echoes of Light" (UC News, 2026-08-08). BLINK has not published an individual page.

name: Jack Walter
title: Programmer
org: University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music (CCM), Lighting Design and Technology
bio: Originally from Canton, Ohio, Jack is a third-year Lighting Design and Technology student at the University of Cincinnati College-Conservatory of Music (CCM) with experience in lighting direction and programming for live music and immersive events. He specializes in MA3 lighting programming and Disguise d3 media server programming. His experience spans a wide range of production environments, including house-of-worship production, systems integration, rental warehouse operations, music festivals and theatre. Most recently, he has worked with touring artists including CAIN and Charli XCX. Outside of his studies, Jack works locally as a contract lighting director with Crossroads Church and is employed by COUR Design in Nashville, Tennessee.
